canonical_append_text: Continuity and discreteness need not compete as universal properties. Under MPF, they may instead be domain-dominated realizations of one shared primitive, P_0, where each becomes primitive within its own domain without being universally primitive. P_Dc := Π_Dc(P_0); P_Dd := Π_Dd(P_0); D_c ≠ D_d. Their lawful distinction is evaluated as D(D_c|D_d), which cannot resolve as a realized zero by the existing Zero-State Domain Membership rule (zero_state ∉ D_domain). At minimum admissible distinction, D(D_c|D_d) <*>_x D(D_c|D_d) =: RT_cd. <*>_x is the existing typed meta-relation operator, not a new family; <=>_r is only a candidate for this specific instantiation. The genuinely open obligations are domain typing, specific operator determination, and a concrete cross-domain invariant. The append excludes identity, universal non-conflict, retrospective domain splitting, and external physical derivation.
